questions.question: Explain why an annuity due always has a higher present value than an ordinary annuity with the same payment, rate, and number of periods.
questions.answerText: Each payment of an annuity due arrives one period earlier, so every cash flow earns one extra period of interest. Equivalently, the annuity-due value equals the ordinary-annuity value multiplied by (1 + r), which is greater than 1.
